excerpt: A denied injury claim is not the end. How to read the denial letter, what to gather, and the appeal and bad faith routes available.
keyTakeaways: A denied claim is not the end. Steps include reviewing the denial letter, gathering evidence, filing appeals, bad faith complaints, or lawsuits. Georgia's bad faith statute (O.C.G.A. § 33-4-6) imposes penalties up to 50% plus attorney fees with a 60-day demand letter requirement. South Carolina's Act (S.C. Code § 38-59-20) requires no pre-suit demand. Georgia's 2-year SOL and South Carolina's 3-year SOL are not extended by a denial.

faqs.question: Why was my claim denied?
faqs.answer: Common reasons include disputed liability, pre-existing conditions, treatment gaps, missed deadlines, policy exclusions, and insufficient evidence. The denial letter should state the reason.

faqs.question: Can I appeal a denied claim?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most insurers have an internal appeals process. Your attorney can submit additional evidence and challenge the reasoning. If the appeal fails, you can file a complaint with the state insurance commissioner or sue.

faqs.question: What is bad faith denial in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Under O.C.G.A. § 33-4-6, unreasonable denial allows recovery of the claim plus up to 50% in penalties and attorney fees. Georgia requires a 60-day demand letter before filing.

faqs.question: What is bad faith denial in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: S.C. Code § 38-59-20 prohibits unreasonable denial, delay, or undervaluation. Remedies include claim value, consequential damages, and potentially punitive damages. No pre-suit demand is required.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a lawsuit?
faqs.answer: Georgia: 2 years from date of injury (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33). South Carolina: 3 years (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). The denial does not restart or extend these deadlines.

faqs.question: Should I hire a lawyer after a denial?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. A denied claim is not the end. An attorney can identify the issue, gather evidence, file appeals, pursue bad faith claims, and take the case to trial. We handle denied claims on contingency — you pay nothing unless we recover.
